items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: I started messing with the saxophone like my father, and so I started playing a tenor.

ctx.x: We are filming today for Hamilton College and we’re developing a Jazz Archive. We are blessed to have with us Bobby Watson, an incredible saxophone artist, who is going to perform for us tonight. Bobby, tell us a little bit about how you got started playing the sax. How old were you?

Well I started in music when I was ten years old. My father, he made a living flying airplanes and worked for the FAA. In fact he was one of the first blacks to become an inspector, the ones that go in and get the black box when a plane crashes in the country. But the way he worked his way through grammar school, he tuned pianos and repaired instruments, and he played saxophone. He played the tenor. So I heard him playing at night, when he wanted to unwind a little bit, and although he never pursued it as a…
remember that. And “Amen, Amen” as it was over. And so I’ve always been connected to playing in the church mainly.
